A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, five figures, four tables, and Appendices A–M. The revisions and relocated content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original Pythia-2.8b preference-learning experiments on OASST and Anthropic HH in Section 6, plus the optimization comparison in Appendix M.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and results in Section 6 and Appendix M. Retained results still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The WRO objectives, games, regularization, and described SFT/DPO/RLHF procedures are retained. Section 5.2 revises the displayed SFT loss expression, but the stated procedure remains maximum-likelihood fitting of preferred samples.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OASST and Anthropic HH and retain the same toy preference scenarios in Appendix F. V2 adds no evaluated dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains SFT, DPO, RLHF, and oracle logit-win-rate optimization. Table 1 retains the same WRO-KL variants, and Appendix M retains the same optimized versus non-optimized comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain Pythia-2.8b, oracle preference relabeling and evaluation, the same h and beta settings, and evaluation on 100 test prompts. The training, preprocessing, and checkpoint-selection settings in Appendices K–L are unchanged.

E4.justification: The loss-versus-win-rate analysis, target-distribution illustrations, DPO counterexamples, and Appendix M comparison of retaining versus dropping the anchor-reward term are all retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same parenthesized quantities, and Section 6.3 retains the same Spearman and Kolmogorov–Smirnov testing. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1 and 4, plotted content of Figures 1–5, and reported statistical findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains HH RLHF win rate 70.46 (0.87) at beta = 0.001.

T1.justification: The central characterization is substantively revised: Definition 3.2 fixes h before quantifying over singleton environments, and Proposition 3.3 explicitly assumes discrete support. Appendix B replaces the brief two-point-mixture argument with new Lemma B.1, an induction, and an explicit argument for both directions. Section 5.2 also revises the mathematical SFT loss expression.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and discussion retain the same headline claims about win rate, WRO/non-WRO distinctions, and optimization difficulty. The formal scope qualification is introduced in Proposition 3.3 and Appendix B without revising those headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains that extending the characterization to continuous densities requires additional convergence assumptions on the evaluation functional. This supplies a substantive applicability boundary absent from v1; interpretations of the empirical results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices K–L retain the judge prompt, temperature scaling, data processing, optimizer settings, learning rates, batch sizes, and checkpoint instructions. No implementation or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Siththaranjan et al. (2024) concerning Bradley–Terry limitations and Shirali et al. (2025) concerning heterogeneous preferences, with corresponding references. The broader positioning and novelty claims are retained.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization is largely preserved. V2 makes localized wording and heading edits, expands the exposition in Appendix B, and adds a short Impact Statement and proceedings information.

P2.justification: V2 repositions Figure 1 within page 6 and changes surrounding text and appendix layout through reflow. The existing figures, captions, and table structures retain their content and design; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the central theorem more precise and easier to check through the discrete-support qualification, clearer quantification of h, and rewritten Appendix B argument. The gain in rigor remains limited: new Lemma B.1 states a countable-support result, while its induction only establishes finite support.
